title: Output Validity Watchdog: config & model-change triggered schema-eval system
creator: Priya Desai
description: Build an automated watchdog that runs targeted structured-output evaluations whenever a model binary or serving configuration (batching, quantization profile, kernel override, prompt-template, runtime flag) changes. Goal: detect regressions in JSON schema adherence and key-field correctness early in the rollout pipeline and provide actionable alerts and simple mitigations (pause rollout, automatic fallback to previous model variant, or create urgent fix tickets).
acceptance_criteria: On any model or serving config change, the system computes a delta and triggers an eval job within 5 minutes for the affected routes.

Evaluations include: schema-violation rate, per-field precision/recall for key extraction fields, structural integrity checks (missing fields, wrong types, truncated arrays), and a lightweight token-distribution divergence metric.
Alerting: violations above configurable thresholds generate an automated incident ticket, Slack alert to #runtime-ops, and annotate the rollout with failure reasons.
Integrations: results are stored in Console telemetry and surfaced on per-route rollout pages with example failing samples and linked PRs or config diffs.
False positive rate on the golden prompt set should be below 3% after heuristics and known transient filters are applied.
notes: 2026-01-18: Kickoff — scoped watchdog to cover model binary changes and serving config commits in the infra repo. Priya and Liam defined initial signal set: schema_violation_rate, field_f1, truncation_count, token_kl.

2026-01-20: Prototype — lightweight runner that replays 500 golden prompts against changed variant and baseline; stores per-sample annotations in S3. Initial run completes in 32s on CI runners (good).

2026-01-22: Decision — use a hybrid sampling strategy: deterministic fingerprint sampling for high-priority customers + reservoir sampling for broad coverage. Trade-off: deterministic sampling eases triage at cost of slightly higher runtime complexity.
2026-01-25: Design review — Mei Chen provided Console mockups for error grouping and sample triage UI. UX request: show field-level diffs and example tokens that changed type or were truncated.

2026-01-27: Performance trade-offs — running full structured parsers on 10k samples is too costly; agreed to run fast JSON-schema validation and spot-check full parsers on the top 1% of failing samples.
2026-01-28: Alert thresholds — initial threshold set to 0.5% schema violation or 5 point drop in field F1. Agreed to add a sliding window to avoid noisy single-commit alarms.
2026-01-30: PR submitted for CI integration and webhook triggers. Linked PR below. Need infra review for secrets and S3 access patterns.

2026-02-01: QA — found false positives for nested arrays when model emits empty-array vs omitted-field. Adjusted heuristic to treat empty-array as tolerated when schema "items" nullable pattern present.
2026-02-02: PM sign-off on MVP scope; moving to canary integration. Next: run for 2 weeks on internal feature routes and tune thresholds based on observed baseline variance.
